transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-09-10 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~54 min
- Attendees: Marcus (Redwood AE), Riley (Redwood SE), Anika (CTO), Diego (Lead ML Eng), Sara (PM)

Summary:
Redwood ran a hands-on hosted API demo focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming behavior, common generation params (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop), and retry/backoff strategies. Customer is evaluating Redwood for a patient-facing summarization feature; main concerns were latency P95 targets, token costs, and PHI handling (encryption/KMS, audit logs).

Topics covered:
- Quick intro + Polaris use case (summaries in clinical app)
- Live hosted API demo: streaming vs non-streaming
- Parameter effects (temp/top_p/max_tokens/stop/stream) and tradeoffs for determinism vs creativity
- Retry/backoff strategies and idempotency keys; how to resume streams
- Console/Optimize suggestions: batching, prefix caching, quantization guidance
- Security/GDPR/SOC2 and private options (Redwood Private/VPC)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Marcus (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Marcus from Redwood, this is Riley our SE, we'll do a quick sandpit demo of the hosted api and then cover patterns for streaming and retries, sound ok?
[00:10] Anika (CTO): yes thanks, excited, short context — we're building a patient notes summarizer, need p95 < 600ms for short queries, and of course PHI encryption concerns.
[00:22] Riley (Redwood SE): great, thanks Anika. quick note: demo will use our hosted chat endpoint, streaming on, and i'll show how params change behavior and how we recommend backoff + fallback to cheaper model variants.
[00:35] Diego (Lead ML Eng): couple quick Qs, are we able to pin model versions? and how does kv cache affect latency if users request similar patient histories?
[00:45] Riley: yes you can pin versions, and we have prefix / kv cache that saves earlier token generations — in practice similar queries can see sub 2x token cost reductions depending on hit rate. cache TTLs are configurable.
[01:05] Sara (PM): also curious about streaming resume — if client disconnects mid-stream, can we pick up where we left off?
[01:12] Riley: short answer: yes, you can use the stream resume token pattern we discussed — we surface partial chunks and the SDK has helpers. if you need exactly at-most-once semantics we recommend idempotency keys plus a server-side buffer to stitch.
[02:00] Marcus: ok we'll jump into the console and then show a curl example. Riley, want to start the live call?
[02:08] Riley: sure — starting a generation with stream:true, temperature:0.2, max_tokens:150... (typing noises)
[02:25] Riley: you can see the response chunks arriving, first chunk at ~80ms, subsequent tokens streaming. note that streaming lowers time-to-first-byte but total tokens cost is same as non-stream — it's a UX/latency improvement.
[03:00] Diego: i'm seeing a faster ttfb than we expected, are you on a cpu or gpu-backed host?
[03:08] Riley: hosted uses optimized GPU runtime with attention kernels; for short chats we often hit under 200ms ttfb for 64-token outputs in our US region, depending on model size and batch timing.
[04:00] Anika: re: cost — is there a way to trade some latency for lower unit cost?
[04:10] Marcus: yes, two levers: 1) model routing to cheaper quantized variants, 2) batching and prefix caching. use Redwood Optimize for suggested batching windows based on your traffic pattern.
[05:00] Riley: showing console Optimize tab now — it suggested batching 50-100ms windows and a quantization profile for the 7B family that keeps quality within 1% of references on our evals.
[06:05] Sara: can you demo a retry scenario, like we hit a transient 503?
[06:12] Riley: sure — best practice is exponential backoff with jitter, keep idempotency keys for not re-applying stateful ops, and for streams we suggest a resume token. I'll simulate a failure... (short silence)  
[06:40] Riley: simulated transient error — client sees a brief 502 then reconnects, service returns last successful chunk id, we request resume(token) and get the rest. Note: if you care about exactly once, combine server-side de-dupe with idempotency key.
[07:15] Diego: what's your recommended backoff schedule?
[07:20] Riley: typically 100ms, 250ms, 600ms with full-jitter and cap at ~2s; also combine with circuit-breaker on a per-route basis so you don't hammer a saturated model pool.
[08:10] Marcus: i want to call out cost telemetry — Console shows token-level cost and perc-route breakdown so product teams can see which prompts are expensive.
[09:00] Anika: in our environment PHI policies require KMS-managed keys, audit logs retention for 7 years, and SSO with SCIM. is that supported?
[09:12] Marcus: yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM, we have audit logs and SCIM SSO; i'll share SOC2 + compliance docs after the call.
[10:00] Riley: back to params — temp: lower gives deterministic outputs, top_p restricts sampling mass, max_tokens caps token charge. small change: if you set stop tokens intelligently you can avoid extra tokens for suffixes.
[11:05] Diego: any heuristics for stop tokens in clinical summaries? sometimes patients' free text has odd punctuation.
[11:15] Riley: combine regex-based cleaning upstream, then set a short stop like ['

', '###'] — and use length penalty or max_new_tokens to avoid runaway. also consider dynamic max_tokens based on previous message length.
[12:30] Anika: what about concurrency — our app does 500 reqs/minute with spiky patterns.
[12:40] Marcus: for spiky loads Dedicated capacity or burst pools are options; for hosted we recommend autoscaling policies plus routing policies that fall back to lower-cost regions or model variants if latency SLOs begin to slip.
[13:15] Sara: show us how to change params in curl vs SDK?
[13:20] Riley: sure — curl payload example with 'stream:true' and 'temperature:0.1' ... (Riley pastes snippet in chat) there's also an SDK helper that wraps reconnection logic.
[15:00] Marcus: quick note on mis-transcriptions — sometimes the console logs 'kv cache' as 'k v cache' in exported traces, tiny mismatch but search still works.
[15:30] Anika: can we use model ensembles or reranking to improve clinical accuracy?
[15:40] Riley: yes, reranking is supported — generate N candidates then use a reranker model or rule-based scoring; Redwood has a reranking API and you can chain it in the Console flow or via the SDK.
[17:00] Diego: is rate limiting per API key or per account?
[17:05] Marcus: options for both — per-key quotas for dev teams, and account-level limits for production tenants; also soft-bursting for sudden surges.
[18:30] Anika: security question — how do you handle retention for telemetry and logs?
[18:40] Marcus: telemetry defaults to 30 days but enterprise packages allow custom retention and export hooks to S3 or GCS for audit retention. we'll share the doc.
[20:00] Riley: demoing a failure-mode playbook in the Console — how to create fallback policies, e.g., if p95>700ms route to a smaller model or toggle streaming off to preserve throughput.
[22:00] Diego: can we automate rollbacks if quality drops after a rollout?
[22:10] Riley: yes, rollouts support automatic metrics-based rollback tied to eval suites — if chat f1 or manual evals slide, you can automatically roll back to prior model.
[24:30] Sara: any gotchas for batching with low-latency chat? worried batching increases latency jitter.
[24:40] Riley: right tradeoff — small micro-batches (20-50ms) reduce cost and add minimal jitter; Console Optimize suggests exact windows based on real traffic traces. For strict p95 constraints prefer prefix caches first.
[26:00] Marcus: let's discuss a proposed pilot: 30-day hosted trial with 100k tokens, run 1k sample prompts, do latency/quality bench, then propose an SOW for Dedicated if numbers look good.
[26:15] Anika: that fits our timeline, we'd need bench results and security docs first.
[27:00] Riley: i'll setup benchmark run, you'll get a report with P50/P95/P99 and token cost breakout.
[28:00] Diego: small nit: can you include cold-starts in the benchmark? some of our instances have complex patient context.
[28:12] Riley: yes — we'll include end-to-end with cold KV cache and a warmed cache scenario.
[30:00] Marcus: switching to common objection zone — cost vs latency, and model ownership concerns. customers sometimes ask if they should host their own. our pitch: Redwood gives consistent SLA and ops tools so teams avoid building and maintaining inference infra.
[31:20] Anika: okay but we have strict on-prem rules for PHI. how invasive is Redwood Private?
[31:30] Marcus: Redwood Private is installable into your VPC, or on-prem air-gapped with our support bundle; there is an enterprise checklist — i'll attach it.
[33:00] Riley: showing more of the Console: tracing hooks per token, error analysis UI, and per-route cost graph. you can also annotate prompts to link to product stories.
[35:00] Diego: any limits on model size for streaming? we plan to try a 70B for high-fidelity summaries.
[35:12] Riley: streaming works with larger models but expect higher TTFB; for heavy-scale production we often recommend a 7B or 13B quantized variant for most requests and reserve 70B for heavy-tail cases via routing.
[36:40] Marcus: last section: retries deep dive — ids, jitter, circuit-breakers, and resumable streams. Riley, do a quick pseudo-code snippet?
[36:50] Riley: pseudo-code: try request with idempotencyKey, on transient error sleep random(100,250)ms, retry up to 4 tries; if streaming, request resume with lastChunkId. don't retry non-idempotent side-effect calls.
[39:00] Anika: any compliance differences between hosted and private?
[39:10] Marcus: hosted supports SOC2 and encrypted-at-rest, but Private is required when customer-managed keys and stricter data residency are mandatory.
[40:00] Sara: final feature ask — can the console surface per-customer cost breakdown for multi-tenant apps?
[40:10] Riley: yes, per-token attribution is supported and you can tag requests with customer_id to split cost.
[41:30] Marcus: ok wrapping up — we'll send the SOC2, KMS notes, and pricing. Riley will run the benchmarks; Diego will send prompt set.
[42:00] Anika: thanks both — quick aside, small transcription hiccup earlier, said 'kv cache' as 'k v cache' — we saw that in the export.
[42:10] Marcus: noted, will include guidance on searching traces.
[43:00] Diego: any rough numbers for quantized 7B vs 70B cost per 1k tokens?
[43:10] Marcus: approximate: quant 7B ~ $0.30/1k tokens, 70B ~ $2.50/1k tokens (ballpark, will confirm in rate card).
[44:00] Sara: ok next steps and ownership?
[44:10] Marcus: i'll send pricing + SOW template (Marcus). Riley will run bench and share results (Riley). Diego to share prompt set (Diego).
[45:00] Anika: heads-up: our legal team will want vendor security questionnaire — expect outreach.
[45:10] Marcus: we'll coordinate with your legal and security.
[46:00] (small cross-talk, wrap-up)
[50:00] Marcus: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and links — meeting ends.
